items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: During that period we both wrote "In the Land of Oo-Bla-Dee". He started it and I helped him a little with it.

ctx.x: He played - not a very good musician but he was more or less a writer, composer, and he had studied all these weird sounds. Often when we had the jazz musicians up here like Sarah Vaughan and all of them, they couldn't stand to hear these chords and things that he was playing. They sounded like discords and whatnot. They'd leave. Milton taught me a great deal. That's the reason I kept up with the times and what was happening. During that period we both wrote "In the Land of Oo-Bla-Dee". He started it and I helped…
When you say you helped a little bit - ?
